The eleven ratings for Hexatronic
Investment memo · Hexatronic (HTRO-SE) · 25 October 2026

Hexatronic: a well-run recovery with a cyclical core, whose upside is concentrated in the next two quarterly reports and is worth about +15% probability-weighted

Prepared 25 October 2026 for Richard; market data at 22 October 2026. Company figures are on the company's own basis, and EPS figures are on the consensus basis, unless stated (Appendix A explains the three EPS bases). Scores run from 1 to 100 against other listed European companies, where 100 is the best.

#0Summary: key insights, implications and conclusions

The bottom line

  1. Own the next two quarterly reports. Hexatronic is likely to beat consensus at its Q4 2026 report on 5 February 2027 (about 70%) and at its Q1 2027 report in late April 2027 (about 65%), because both quarters face easy comparisons.
  2. Re-underwrite the holding at the Q1 2027 report. From Q2 2027 the comparisons harden, supply shortages cap growth, and the probability of estimate cuts rises to about 40% at each report.
  3. Expect about +15%, not +133%. My probability-weighted value at end-2027 is about SEK 47 a share (+15%), my central value SEK 55 (+36%), and my scenario range SEK 26-65. The model's SEK 95.52 counts the same optimism twice.
  4. Manage the position by calendar. The tripwires are external and observable: Corning's and Prysmian's commentary, spot fibre prices, hyperscalers' capex guidance and Hexatronic's own North American growth rate.

The business. Hexatronic is a Swedish maker of passive fibre infrastructure (ducts, microducts, cable and connectivity) with SEK 8.7bn of sales. It is increasingly also a data-centre cabling and installation contractor and a specialist in defence and subsea connectivity.

The recovery. In the eighteen months since an external chief executive arrived, Hexatronic has cut costs, shifted its sales mix toward data centres and defence, repaired its balance sheet and ridden two demand upswings, the rebound in US fibre and the AI data-centre build, from a trough margin of 7.2% to a record one. The shares have risen 113% in twelve months and now trade at their own ten-year median forward multiple.

The case in one sentence. Hexatronic is a cyclical niche specialist in the second year of an upswing, with a structurally lower cost base and a better mix than in its last cycle, whose rate of change peaked in Q3 2026 and whose next two quarterly reports are bounded and likely to beat consensus; the second half of 2027 will either prove the thesis, through a Fiber Solutions margin floor near 10% against hard comparisons, or return the stock to the cyclical template that its own 2023 history and its thin shareholder register would punish quickly.

The seven conclusions that matter.

  1. 1The positive skew is real but short-dated: it lies in the next two quarterly reports. The Q4 2026 report (5 February 2027) is compared with Q4 2025 sales of SEK 1,848m at a 7.2% margin, and the Q1 2027 report (late April 2027) with Q1 2026 sales of SEK 1,698m at 8.6%, a quarter held back by a cold winter. Our base case has sales growing 21% and 23% in those two quarters, with EBITA up roughly 70% and 45% year on year. Three facts support a beat: management's cues have under-stated outcomes for a year (the July 2026 warning of Q3 margin pressure preceded a record margin), the order book covers four months, and management has pre-announced and bounded Data Center's Q4 normalisation. I put the probability of beating the four-contributor consensus at about 70% at the Q4 report and about 65% at the Q1 report. These two reports are where the probability of an upside surprise is unusually skewed to the positive.
  2. 2From Q2 2027 the skew turns negative, and the market has not priced that. From Q2 2027 Hexatronic's North American sales are compared with growth of +44% and +51% a year earlier, Data Center's Q3 2026 timing benefit reverses, and shortages of glass fibre and connectors cap organic growth at about 9% against demand indicators above 12%. Our base case has revenue growth of 11% in Q2 2027 and 5% in Q3 2027. Our range for 2027 EPS is SEK 2.1 to 3.3 around a base of SEK 2.78 (-25% to +18%); weighting the downside at about 27%, the base at 55% and the upside at 18% gives a probability-weighted SEK 2.7. The only published downside case is Redeye's SEK 16 bear framing, and no one has modelled the drop in growth when the comparisons harden.
  3. 3Consensus already sits at our level, so there is no annual upgrade cycle to harvest. Redeye's post-Q3 EPS figures (SEK 2.39, 2.85 and 3.36 for 2026-28) sit on or slightly above ours (SEK 2.38, 2.78 and 3.29). When FactSet absorbs Redeye's update in November, the dashboard will show a +5-9% revision burst; that burst records the Q3 report and carries no new information. The one clear gap is FY2029: the single broker's SEK 4.18 rests on a step up to a 12.1% EBIT margin and on falling depreciation, and nothing in our work supports either (our figure is SEK 3.58).
  4. 4The margin plateaus near 11%, not at the 12% target, and the board's own incentive plan shows that the board expects this. The 2026 long-term incentive plan (LTIP 2026) vests on an average adjusted EBITA margin of 9.8-11.1% over 2026-28; our path averages 10.8%. About 70 of the 260 basis points of margin recovery from 2025 to 2027 come from depreciation dilution (capex running below depreciation), not from operating improvement, and that benefit reverses when the subsea and South Carolina lines commission in 2028-29. The self-help programme is finished. Further margin gains must come from volume on a fixed cost base in Fiber Solutions (30-40% incremental margins), diluted by services and acquired units earning 12-16%.
  5. 5Hexatronic sits in the wrong layer of a very attractive value chain. Demand for fibre is structural in data centres and recovering in the US, but the profit pool and the pricing power sit upstream with five glass makers that hold about 67% of preform capacity. One of those five, Corning, is both Hexatronic's main supplier and a strengthening competitor. Hexatronic's own layer is fragmented, easy to enter in services, and oversupplied in European ducts and, as Orbia's Q2 and Q3 2026 comments show, in US high-density polyethylene (HDPE) conduit too. Hexatronic's current supportive conditions are borrowed from glass scarcity and a cyclical upswing, and they will probably expire around 2028, when new Chinese, Corning and Prysmian capacity arrives.
  6. 6The valuation guideline overstates the case by counting the same optimism twice. The dashboard rule places the stock in the "Reinforcing" phase, with a guideline fair multiple of 22.34x (the stock's ten-year 90th percentile). The model applies that multiple to its pre-amortisation 2029 EPS of SEK 4.28, which gives SEK 95.52 a share and a +133% return. That calculation double-counts: once through the EPS basis (consensus-basis 2029 EPS is SEK 3.58) and once through a multiple the stock reached only when organic growth exceeded 60% in 2021-22. In my view the stock is in a "thesis broadening, not yet reinforcing" phase; its fair band is 13.6-17.6x (the median to the 75th percentile) on consensus-basis EPS, with a central 15.5x; and its 14-month value is SEK 49-63 (central SEK 55, about +36%), against SEK 80 at the guideline multiple on the same EPS.
  7. 7The practical implication: own the two likely beats, then re-underwrite the holding at the Q1 2027 report. The expected return to end-2027 is positive (my probability-weighted value is about SEK 47, +15%), but it combines a high-probability six months with a lower-probability, negatively skewed twelve months. The tripwires are external and observable: Corning's and Prysmian's shipment commentary (two quarters' lead); spot prices for G.652.D and G.657.A2 fibre and connector lead times (one to two quarters' lead on gross margin and on the end of scarcity); hyperscalers' 2027 capex guidance (late January 2027); and Hexatronic's own North American growth rate and Data Center sales on 5 February 2027. A holder beyond April 2027 is underwriting the upside scenario, in which supply eases, orders from the US Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment programme (BEAD) arrive from mid-2027, Data Center holds SEK 650m quarters and 2027 EPS reaches SEK 3.2; that scenario is worth SEK 63-70 a share at 17.6-20x.

Where I differ from the market. I am more positive than the market on the next two reports and more negative on almost everything after them; I am in line on 2027-28 annual EPS.

Scorecard

The four judgements that move the shares most, with the arithmetic

Four judgements carry most of the risk to value over one to two years: North American volume and the Fiber Solutions margin dominate the risk to 2027 EPS and are skewed to the downside, while the multiple is the largest value swing of all.

All EPS figures here are on the consensus basis. Base-case 2027 EPS is SEK 2.78 on about 223m diluted shares at a 26% tax rate, so each SEK 100m of EBITA is worth about SEK 0.33 of EPS.

1. North American Fiber Solutions volume after the refill largest EPS risk

Base case
Volume grows 12% in 2027 on a 2026 base of about SEK 2.5bn: +20-25% in Q1 against the cold-winter base, then +5-10% from Q2.
Leverage
Fiber Solutions' incremental and decremental margins on organic volume are 30-40%.
Adverse case
If the US rebound proves partly a refill of inventories and North American volume falls 20% from Q2 2027 instead of rising, 2027 revenue lands about SEK 500-560m below the base case (roughly 30 points on SEK 1.8-1.9bn of Q2-Q4 sales). At a 35% decremental margin, that removes SEK 175-195m of EBITA and SEK 0.58-0.65 of EPS, and takes 2027 EPS to about SEK 2.1-2.2 (-22% to -24%). The Clinton capacity that management has just retained would be under-absorbed again, and a defensive European consolidation would become likely, with SEK 100-150m of one-off costs that take a further SEK 0.35-0.50 off reported EPS.
Upside mirror
Volume growth of 20% instead of 12% adds SEK 0.25 of EPS.
Early warnings
North American growth falling to single digits before the comparisons harden; Brightspeed's 2027 refinancing (Brightspeed spent USD 5.6bn against a USD 3bn budget); AT&T's USD 1bn cut to 2027-28 capex; Dura-Line's commentary on conduit volume and price.
Probability
The probability of the adverse North American case over 18 months is 20-25%.

2. The level of Data Center sales after Q3 2026 lumpier, less leveraged

Base case
Data Center sales of SEK 550m in Q4 2026 and SEK 2,640m in 2027 (organic growth of 15%, within a range of 5-25%).
Leverage
Services were 39% of segment sales in the first nine months of 2026, so the incremental margin is only 15-25%. Each 10 points of organic growth is worth about SEK 220-265m of revenue, SEK 45-65m of EBITA and SEK 0.15-0.20 of EPS.
Adverse case
A hyperscaler financing pause that cuts growth to 5% costs SEK 0.18 of EPS; a Q4 2026 Data Center print below SEK 500m would signal that pause.
Concentration
One Communication Zone project drove much of Q3's beat, and the company does not disclose how concentrated Data Center's sales are.
Correlation
The probability that at least one of judgements 1 and 2 turns adverse is about 35%, and the probability that both do is about 10%, because both run through US long-term interest rates and the appetite for AI capex.

3. The Fiber Solutions margin as growth slows the pricing question

Base case
A Fiber Solutions margin of 9.4% in 2027 on SEK 5,250m of sales, and 9.8% in 2028. Each 100 basis points is worth SEK 52m of EBITA and SEK 0.17 of EPS.
New evidence
US HDPE conduit prices are under pressure from domestic overcapacity (Orbia, Q2 and Q3 2026; Atkore has exited HDPE pipe), while Hexatronic's US product range stays duct-heavy until its South Carolina cable line runs in 2027. Dura-Line's own precedent in 2024 was rising volumes and falling prices.
Adverse cases
If the 2027 margin stalls at the 2026 level of 8.7%, EPS loses SEK 0.12; if the margin slips to 7% as prices erode on flat volume, EPS loses SEK 0.42.
Floor
The lower cost base gives Fiber Solutions a structural margin floor of 8-9% on flat volume, against 5-6% in 2025, which keeps the downside above 2025's level.

4. The multiple not an EPS item, but the largest value swing

Arithmetic
On two-year-forward consensus-basis EPS of SEK 3.58 at end-2027, each turn of P/E is worth SEK 3.58 a share, or 8.7% of today's price.
Range
A move from 13.8x to the 35th percentile (11.7x) is worth -SEK 7.5 a share (-18%); to the 75th percentile (17.6x), +SEK 13.6 (+33%); to the 10th percentile (8.2x, where the stock sat in 2024-25), -SEK 20 (-49%).
Precedent
In 2023 Hexatronic's multiple fell one to two quarters before its earnings did. With about USD 7m of daily trading, one visible broker and no anchor owner, a 20-35% drawdown on intact fundamentals is plausible; the shares fell 18.7% from their July-August 2026 high on no company news.

Second-order items, which move EPS by SEK 0.10 or less each:

  • A 10% stronger krona removes 9% of reported revenue but only about 3% of EPS (SEK 0.08), because production is local.
  • Each point of tax rate is worth SEK 0.04 of EPS.
  • The SEK 400m-a-year acquisition block adds only about SEK 0.05 of 2027 EPS and SEK 0.10 of 2028 EPS after amortisation and forgone interest, so it matters for the narrative of reaching SEK 11bn of sales, not for EPS.
  • Earn-out revaluations and items affecting comparability add ±SEK 0.10-0.20 a year of noise to reported EPS, with a negative skew.

#1Tailwinds in the operating environment; absence of headwinds

The external environment turned in 2026 from a net headwind into the strongest net tailwind since 2022, but the tailwinds are cyclical, capped by supply, and probably past their peak rate of change.

Evidence. From 2024 to mid-2025 the environment was a net headwind. In 2026 two demand engines that did not exist in the last cycle turned it into a tailwind: the AI data-centre build and the rebuild of US fibre networks. Defence adds a third, smaller tailwind. Against them stand a structurally shrinking European market, a supply constraint, deferred energy orders and a tighter financial regime.

Inference. The tailwinds are cyclical and thematic rather than contracted, and they are front-loaded into 2026-28. The rate of change of Hexatronic's tailwinds probably peaked in Q3 2026: Data Center normalises in Q4, the comparisons harden from Q2 2027, and supply constraints bind.

The configuration is asymmetric. The supply constraint caps the upside, while the two demand channels, US carrier capex and hyperscaler capex, leave the downside open; both channels are also correlated through the long end of the yield curve.

Channel checks suggest that the US surge is mainly end-use demand, with restocking secondary: distributors describe their inventories as "balanced", and Wesco's broadband backlog is up 80%. That evidence is why I keep US growth positive through 2027 rather than reversing it.

So what. Model 2027 organic growth of about 9%, well below Q3 2026's 17%; front-load growth in 2026-27 and taper it thereafter. The two swing variables for 2027 are the end of the US refill and the krona.

The glass shortage binds hardest in bend-insensitive G.657.A2 data-centre fibre and in multi-fibre push-on (MPO) connectors, while the price of standard G.652.D telecom fibre has already fallen from USD 17-18 to USD 11-13 per fibre-km. The shortage therefore hits Data Center's products sooner, and Fiber Solutions' cable costs may ease during 2027.

Strongest counter-case. Both demand engines could run hotter and for longer than I assume. If Data Center held quarters of SEK 650m or more, BEAD orders arrived from mid-2027 into a duct market protected by the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA), and supplier validation lifted the supply cap, 2027 revenue would be about SEK 10.1bn and EPS about SEK 3.2. The sector evidence that data-centre growth slows from 2028, as 230m fibre-km of Chinese preform capacity and Corning's and Prysmian's new US capacity arrive, also helps Hexatronic before it hurts: as a non-integrated buyer of glass, Hexatronic gains from lower input costs before it loses from the end of scarcity.

What would change my view. A Q4 2026 Data Center print above SEK 600m, or North American growth still above 30% in Q1 2027, would raise my 2027 organic growth estimate toward 12%. A hyperscaler capex guide below 2026 levels in late January 2027, or Dura-Line reporting volume declines, would lower it toward 5%.

Market versus me. The market narrative treats the recovery as mainly structural ("less cyclical than fibre to the home") and the supply constraint as a damper. I agree that the data-centre leg is structural and that supply damps growth rather than threatens it in the near term. I differ in two ways: I weight the US leg as cyclical, with a refill component that washes out in 2027, and I treat the two demand channels as one correlated risk, which the narrative does not.

Score: 62. Strong, broad tailwinds for 12 months, but cyclical in quality, capped by supply, past their peak rate of change, and set against a structural European headwind and company-level currency and discount-rate headwinds.

#2Internally-driven corporate change; absence of problems

The internal change is genuine, broad and already in the accounts; the open problems concern people and controls, and they cluster at the moment of scaling.

Evidence. Rikard Fröberg, chief executive since 1 March 2025 (previously at McKinsey, Ahlsell and Ansell), launched a performance programme four months into his tenure. Eighteen months on, the change shows in the profit line: Hexatronic has beaten the consensus it commissions on profit four quarters in a row, by the widest margin in Q3 2026. The open problems form a cluster rather than one large item.

Inference. The internal change is genuine, multi-dimensional and unusually quick to reach the profit line, and it is the part of the case that survives a pause in the external cycle: the lower cost base gives Fiber Solutions a margin floor of 8-9% on flat volume, against 5-6% in 2025.

Three weaknesses offset that strength. Management depth has thinned exactly when scaling, acquisitions and supply management need it most. The self-help programme is complete rather than continuing. And the strategic bridge from today's SEK 8.7bn of sales to the SEK 11bn target is unquantified; we assume SEK 0.8-1.2bn of unannounced acquired revenue by 2028.

The long-term incentive plan is the most informative internal signal: a board that planned for a 12% margin would not set the plan's vesting range at 9.8-11.1%.

So what. Credit Hexatronic with continued acquired growth of 3-6% of sales a year at 5-7x EBITDA (about SEK 400m a year), a structurally higher Fiber Solutions margin floor, and no further margin gains from self-help. Expect no dividend before 2029-30. Carry about 1m shares a year of incentive dilution and a 30% probability of a further directed share issue over four years. Three or more open problems at once is the pattern that argues for discounting the Q3 beat, though not for dismissing it.

Strongest counter-case. The vacancies are being filled from within by people who built the businesses: Wärme has run Data Center's acquisitions since 2022, and Lindén designed the Fiber Solutions programme. Q3 2026, delivered under interim leadership, was the best quarter in three years, and an external CFO arriving mid-way through an acquisition cycle is a known pattern for resetting capital discipline. On this reading the problems are transitional, not structural.

What would change my view. Permanent appointments to the CFO and Data Center roles by the Q4 report (5 February 2027) would remove the largest internal risk. Failure to fill either role by then would widen the range of outcomes and, alongside Harsh Environment and supply, would add a third unexpected problem (a third "cockroach"). A capital markets day setting 2030 targets, more likely in H2 2027 once a CFO is in place, would be the next internal step.

Market versus me. The market narrative credits the cost programme, the mix pivot and the acquisitions fully, and treats the leadership changes lightly (one house mentions them). I agree on the strength of what has been done, but I give more weight to the thinning management bench and to the signal in the incentive range, which nobody else discusses.

Score: 64. Strong, proven, well-resourced change with a clear destination; held below the top tier by thin management depth at the moment of scaling, no capital-return dimension and a self-help programme that is complete rather than continuing.

#3Value chain, business model, financial profile, management

Hexatronic buys scarce glass from concentrated suppliers, one of which competes with it, and sells into fragmented, oversupplied layers; its protections are real but narrow, and its financial profile is that of a mid-quality cyclical industrial.

Evidence, value chain. Upstream, glass preform is concentrated: five makers hold about 67% of capacity, and only ten to twelve companies draw glass. Downstream, where Hexatronic sells, the market is fragmented. Hexatronic has about 1% of the US market, 2,133 employees against Prysmian's 33,000, and is not number one or two in any large market it serves. Customer concentration is low: the largest customer is below 4% of sales.

Evidence, financial profile. Hexatronic's financial profile combines high operating leverage in both directions with mediocre returns and heavy working capital, offset by a comfortable balance sheet.

Evidence, management. Management is assessed in #2: an enabling chief executive with an eighteen-month record of acting, and a strategy that spans three cycles that do not move together (US fibre, data centres, and defence and energy). Pay is modest (SEK 9.4m), the chief executive has put his own money into savings shares, and management owns about 6% of the company. Governance meets the minimum standard: six independent directors, thin director holdings, no internal audit, PwC as auditor since 2013, and the chair's call options issued by Accendo. Communication is honest about near-term caution but withholds the transmission mechanism: the company gives no numeric guidance, order intake, book-to-bill ratio or split of price and volume.

Inference. The industry structure is supportive now in the US and in data centres, but that support is borrowed from a temporary scarcity of glass and of compliant local capacity, not earned through Hexatronic's own position. Structurally, Hexatronic is a price-taker on inputs and in both European and US ducts, protected only by niche system-selling, local capacity, certifications and a contracted step-up in subsea capacity.

The financial profile is that of a mid-quality cyclical industrial: high operating leverage in both directions, moderate margins with a ceiling below the last peak, mediocre returns, heavy working capital and comfortable debt.

Management is the strongest of the three legs, and it is dynamic rather than enlightened. Its capital-allocation record is improving (cheap acquisitions, equity raised near the share-price high, partner-backed capex), but the 2021-23 capacity build at the top of the last cycle is still in the base, and the company has no capital-return lever.

So what. Treat Hexatronic as a cyclical niche specialist with a mix tailwind, not as a compounder. Margins can reach 11-12% in a strong year but should not be modelled at peer-leading levels; pricing should be modelled as cost pass-through with a one-quarter lag; and US share gains should fade once the majors' new capacity arrives in 2028. The right fair multiple lies in the cyclical-recovery band, not the serial-acquirer band (HMS Networks trades at 24x after proving 17 acquisitions since 2012).

Strongest counter-case. Hexatronic's narrow moats are exactly the ones that matter in a US build constrained by labour and protected by local-content rules, and the company keeps winning there (North America +80%, against Dura-Line's +23-30%). The pivot to services, defence and subsea raises the structural margin floor; three cheap acquisitions a year at mid-teens returns compound quietly; and the re-cabling of data centres every two to three years could become a recurring revenue base that nobody has yet measured.

What would change my view. Disclosure of realised price premia on BABA-compliant duct, or of mix gains from allocating scarce products, would show real pricing power. A Fiber Solutions margin above 10% through the hard comparisons of H2 2027 would show that the margin floor is structural rather than cyclical. Return on invested capital sustained above 15% would raise the quality grade.

Market versus me. Redeye's framing has moved from a "35% discount to peers" to "9x EV/EBITA 2027e, no longer a deep discount", which is a fair reading of the business quality; online forums treat Hexatronic as a data-centre growth story. I agree with the broker on quality and disagree with the growth-story framing: Hexatronic is a volume seller, not a scarcity seller, and it buys from its competitors.

Score: 45. Strong, dynamic management and a sensible strategy sit on a competitive downstream layer with no upstream position, mediocre returns, heavy working capital and a margin ceiling below the last peak.

#4Conservative guidance; conservative sell-side expectations; track record of delivery and upgrades

Since its September 2025 rebasing, Hexatronic has given conservative cues and beaten them every quarter; but with no numeric guidance there is nothing formal to raise, and the record is cyclical.

Evidence. The company gives no numeric annual guidance. It sets destination targets for 2028 (acquisitions included) and gives qualitative cues for the next quarter.

The September 2025 rebasing cut the targets, softened the outlook for fibre to the home (FTTH), took SEK 298m of one-off charges and moved the FTTH metric to homes passed. Sceptics called the rebasing kitchen-sinking, and the over-delivery since then is consistent with that reading. Since the rebasing, the cues have been conservative: a July 2026 warning of Q3 margin pressure preceded an 11.3% margin, and the Q4 2026 normalisation was pre-announced. The targets have been held, not raised, through three beats.

The 2028 targets sit about 10% above the broker's 2028 revenue forecast (Redeye, SEK 10,213m), mainly because the broker excludes unannounced acquisitions, and above the broker's margin forecast of about 11.7-11.8%.

Before 2025 the record was poor. Hexatronic missed in Q1 2024, Q4 2024 and Q1 2025, and issued a profit warning with its Q2 2025 miss; FY2026 consensus EPS was cut from SEK 5.05 to 1.76, and the broker's base-case value from SEK 57 to SEK 24.

Estimates have risen 12-27% over twelve months but were flat over the one and three months before the Q3 report (revision score 11). The share of analysts recommending a buy is 75%, after a 50-point rise in six months, and the mean target price has risen 36% in six months.

Inference. Management's behaviour has shifted from over-promising to tracking honestly with conservative cues. Without numbers, however, there is nothing formal to raise, so the "upgrade" mechanism is a results surprise against a bar that the company itself sets through a four-name consensus.

The near-term cues are more likely to under-state than to over-state outcomes. The destination targets are moderately conservative in Data Center (on course a year early), about right in Fiber Solutions and stretched in Harsh Environment, and the group's 12% margin target is realistic only if Harsh Environment reaches 15%. The record is cyclical: beats in upswings, misses in downswings, and in 2023 the turn came faster than the forecasts.

So what.

  • Lean above pre-Q3 consensus for the next two to three quarters.
  • Lean below the 12% target on the 2028-30 margin, toward the incentive range.
  • Expect 2026 estimates to settle around SEK 2.39-2.45, and 2027 estimates to move by low single digits after each of the next two reports.
  • Expect the first cautious cue at the Q2 or Q3 2027 report: I put the probability of a cue that reads as a reduction at 35-40% at each of those reports, against 10-15% at each of the next two.
  • Do not treat the single broker's FY2029 figure as "the market's view".

Strongest counter-case. The pattern of conservative cues and beats has run for four quarters and reinforces itself while the US and data-centre cycles run; the company has beaten through a European decline of 9-31% and through a supply constraint. The Data Center target could be raised (about 30% probability within 18 months, most likely at a capital markets day setting 2030 targets), and a second broker initiating coverage on FactSet would broaden the base for revisions.

What would change my view. A Q4 2026 report in line with consensus rather than ahead of it (Data Center below SEK 530m or a Fiber Solutions margin below 8.5%) would end the beat pattern earlier than I expect. A return to numeric annual guidance would change the mechanics of upgrades entirely.

Market versus me. The broker expects Q1 2027 to beat, as I do. The market narrative misses the point that the FY2026 EPS base contains SEK 0.23 of one-off gain, so it understates the clean 2027 EPS growth rate (+26%); the market will read reported growth of +17%. On the 2028 targets, the broker and the board's incentive range already discount the 12% margin, so the practical gap to "guidance" is small.

Score: 58. Cues are conservative and the recent beat record is strong, but there is no numeric guidance to raise, coverage is effectively one model, the record before 2025 was poor and the comparisons harden from mid-2027.

#5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out scope, feedback loops

Operating leverage drives the next two years' numbers in both directions; pricing power is nominal, financial leverage a modest tailwind, the cost-out largely spent, and the feedback loops turn from reinforcing to balancing in 2028.

Evidence and inference, mechanism by mechanism.

  • Operating leverage: the most important mechanism, and it works both ways. Fiber Solutions (58% of sales) is a plant business: raw materials are 60-65% of sales, and incremental and decremental margins on organic volume are 30-40% (in Q3 2026, about SEK 174m of organic sales growth produced SEK 66m of extra EBITA, 38%). Data Center (28% of sales) is 39% services with variable labour, so its incremental margin is 15-25%; Harsh Environment's (16% of sales) is 25-30%. The blended group incremental margin is about 25-28% on organic volume, and about 20% on total revenue growth, because half of 2026's growth was acquired at 12-15% margins. That arithmetic is why the group margin lands at 10% in 2026 rather than snapping back to the mid-teens, and why the margin ceiling in this cycle is 11-12%, not 16-17%: the European duct plants that carried the 2022 peak are not returning to full absorption. Reversing the Clinton downsizing puts fixed cost back into the base and raises operating leverage in both directions.
  • Pricing power: nominal, not real. The US price increases of 2026 were glass-linked surcharges on cable and industry-wide pass-through; Hexatronic's main US product, HDPE duct, faces price pressure from domestic overcapacity; European microduct prices fall with volume; and management withholds the magnitudes. The adjusted gross margin moved from 41.4% (Q4 2024) to 37.5% (H2 2025), 38.7% (Q2 2026) and 39.8% (Q3 2026): protected and recovering, not expanding. Real pricing power exists only in defence connectors, subsea and, while the shortage lasts, data-centre hardware (15-20% of sales), and it is worth at most 50-100 basis points of group gross margin in 2026-27. Contracts indexed to input costs with a one-quarter lag work in both directions: falling input costs in 2027-28 give a brief gross-margin tailwind and then hand it back.
  • Financial leverage: low, and a modest tailwind. Net interest falls from SEK 200m (2024) and SEK 151m (2025) to about SEK 105m (2026) and SEK 80-95m (2027-28), worth 2-3 points a year of EPS growth. Net debt excluding leases stays at about SEK 1.1bn at end-2026 and end-2027, even after SEK 400m a year of acquisitions, and falls toward SEK 0.5bn (0.3x) by 2029. The balance sheet therefore becomes under-levered, and a decision on capital returns or a larger acquisition becomes a 2029-30 event.
  • Cost-out scope: largely used. The SEK 120m programme is in the 2026 run-rate (about SEK 90-100m of year-on-year savings in 2026 and SEK 10-20m of residual savings in 2027). Scale takes operating costs from 25% of sales to about 24% by 2028: about 100 basis points gross, and 50-70 basis points net of returning costs (Clinton, the South Carolina start-up and technician wage inflation of 4% or more). A further European duct consolidation (SEK 50-100m of savings for SEK 100-150m of one-off cost) is a response to a downside scenario, not a base-case lever, because the shift to connection products needs the plants.
  • Feedback loops: reinforcing through mid-2027, balancing in 2028-30. Three loops reinforce now: US absorption (volume lifts the Fiber Solutions margin toward 10%, which funds the retention of capacity, which wins share as BEAD begins); data-centre services (installation leads to day-2 services and re-cabling); and acquisition funding (a share valued at 14x earnings buys service companies at 5-7x, the HMS Networks pattern, which stops working below a valuation of about 9-10x). Four loops balance: scarcity (which caps volume and builds working capital); European overcapacity (prices fall with volume); working capital (growth absorbs SEK 230-260m per SEK 1bn, so free cash flow after leases is only about 68% of net income in 2027); and the capacity cycle (Chinese preform, Corning's 50% expansion, Prysmian's doubling of US fibre capacity from H2 2028, plus Sterlite and HFCL, all arriving as data-centre optical growth is expected to slow from 2028). The observable signal that turns the loops is a fall in spot fibre prices and lead times, which reaches the gross margin about one quarter later.

So what. Revenue growth still produces outsized profit growth, but less than in the last cycle and less than the headline suggests. Adjusted EBITA grows 39% in 2026 on 15% revenue growth, 21% in 2027 on 11.5% and 15% in 2028 on 11.5%, then 7% and 9% in 2029-30.

Reported EPS grows two to three points a year more slowly than EBITA (about +17%, +18%, +9% and +11% for 2027-30), because amortisation of acquired intangibles rises from SEK 100m to SEK 140m and the share count is 8% higher after the May 2026 issue. On the consensus basis, the 2023 EPS peak of SEK 4.17 is not regained until about 2030, even though EBITA passes its 2023 level in 2028. About 70 basis points of the 2025-27 margin recovery is depreciation dilution, which reverses in 2028-29.

Strongest counter-case. Dura-Line earns a 16-17% EBITDA margin at full utilisation, and management attributes Hexatronic's gap to utilisation and key-account pricing, so US operating leverage has further to run if volume holds. Scarcity could let Hexatronic prioritise data-centre, subsea and defence orders and so improve its mix, and the services loop could make Data Center more recurring than any contractor peer.

What would change my view. A disclosed split of price and volume showing real price gains above cost; a Fiber Solutions margin above 10% in a quarter with flat North American volume; or a Data Center margin holding above 16% through Q4's reversal of product timing.

Market versus me. The sell side reads the Fiber Solutions recovery as structural, and the Q3 margin as proof that services do not dilute the margin. I read the recovery as half structural (the cost base) and half cyclical (volume absorption against a price headwind), and the Q3 margin as a mix effect that reverses when product timing turns. Nobody else makes the depreciation-dilution point.

Score: 55. Material two-way operating leverage and falling interest give outsized profit growth for two years, but there is no real pricing power, the cost-out is spent, and the reinforcing loops depend on external conditions and are dated.

Cash. After acquisitions, free cash flow is near zero in 2027 and SEK 200-450m a year in 2028-30. The equity story is EPS growth and de-leveraging, not cash return.

Inference. Revenue compounds at about 11% a year to 2030, half organic and half acquired, against about 26% a year in 2019-25, growth that was front-loaded into the FTTH boom. Revenue growth is double-digit every year to 2029 and high single digits in 2030.

Margins stay higher than in 2024-25 and lower than in 2022-23 throughout the forecast: they plateau at 11-11.5% in 2027-28 and drift to about 11% as competitors' capacity lands and services grow. EPS growth is strongest in 2026-28 (+17-27% a year on the consensus basis from the clean base) and slows to about 9-11% in 2029-30.

Against consensus, our forecasts differ in three ways. On a like-for-like organic basis we are within 1-2% of the broker for 2027-28 on both revenue and EPS (Redeye SEK 2.85 and 3.36 post-Q3, against our 2.78 and 3.29). On reported revenue we are 3-10% above, because we include unannounced acquisitions. On FY2029 EPS we are about 14% below the single broker.

Against the 2028 targets, our base case falls short everywhere except Data Center, yet lands in the upper half of the board's incentive range.

Strongest counter-case. The upside scenario (about 20% probability) would meet the group's 12% margin target in 2028, with SEK 11.5bn of sales and EPS of SEK 3.9. The table below sets the upside and downside scenarios against the base case; the downside would probably also bring SEK 100-150m of restructuring one-offs.

What would change my view within six months. Data Center sales in Q4 2026 below SEK 500m or above SEK 600m; North American Fiber Solutions growth below 20% in Q4 2026; group organic growth below 15% in Q1 2027; a glass or connector allocation cut disclosed as lost revenue; or an acquisition above EUR 50m or a directed share issue.

Market versus me. We are in line with the market for 2026-28 EPS, above it on reported revenue (because we include acquisitions) and below it for 2029 (because we see no margin step and expect the capacity cycle). The difference in the composition of growth matters more than the difference in its level: we see half-acquired growth with a margin plateau, where the narrative sees organic growth with a margin on its way to 12%.

Score: 60. Double-digit revenue growth every year to 2029 and EPS growth of 17-27% a year to 2028 from a depressed base; held back by a margin that plateaus below the last peak, growth that is half bought, and a range of outcomes that is wide and modestly negatively skewed from mid-2027.

#7Scope for forecasts to lead to upgrades to guidance, estimates and narrative over 6-12 months

The favourable gap is concentrated in the next six months, and it comes from beating a thin, company-set consensus, not from upgrades to annual estimates, which already sit at our level.

Evidence. The dashboard's revision data show EPS revisions of 0-1% over one and three months, +4% over six months and +16% over twelve months; the mean target price is up 36% over six months, and 75% of analysts recommend a buy. FactSet's weekly mean EPS figures (SEK 2.26, 2.67 and 3.07 for 2026-28 at 16 October) pre-date the Q3 report. Redeye's post-Q3 figures are SEK 2.39, 2.85 and 3.36, with a base-case value of SEK 46 (up from SEK 44). Redeye's quarterly path has Q4 2026 sales of SEK 2,254m at a 9.6% margin (Data Center SEK 582m), Q1 2027 sales of SEK 2,038m with SEK 217m of EBITA, and Q2 2027 sales of SEK 2,563m. Our quarterly base case is above Redeye's on the Q4 2026 margin (10.1% against 9.6%, with Fiber Solutions above 9% against the broker's 8.0%) and slightly above on Q1 2027 sales.

Inference, event by event. The probability of upgrades is high until the Q1 2027 report and then gives way to the probability of cuts.

Guidance. The cues at the Q4 and Q1 reports are likely to stay cautious and be beaten; the first cautious cue that reads as a reduction is likely at the Q2 or Q3 2027 report. The only target that could be raised is Data Center's (about 30% probability), probably through a 2030 framework at a capital markets day rather than by lifting the 2028 target.

Narrative. The recovery story is about two thirds told. The steps ahead in the next six months (a record year above the 2023 revenue peak, Fiber Solutions near a 10% margin, management appointments, more bolt-on acquisitions, the first BEAD orders) are driven by results and of moderate novelty. The contracted, high-novelty step, the subsea capacity, is a 2028 event.

So what. The favourable gap is concentrated in the next six months, and it is about beating a thin, company-set consensus, not about upgrades to annual estimates. By end-April 2027, FY2027 consensus is likely to sit within ±5% of SEK 2.85 and FY2028 consensus within ±5% of today's level; FY2029 consensus is likely to be cut 10-15% toward SEK 3.6-3.8 whenever a second broker publishes or the single broker rolls its model forward.

The narrative risk is that the market reads Q4 Data Center normalisation or a slowing US growth rate as the end of the story. The narrative opportunity is that Hexatronic proves it can grow through 2027 with a structurally higher margin floor, which would support the argument that its changed mix deserves a higher multiple.

Strongest counter-case. A second or third broker initiating coverage (more likely after a CFO appointment or a capital markets day) would widen the base for revisions, and could bring a Nordic serial-acquirer framing (the HMS Networks template) that re-rates the stock regardless of the quarter. Data Center sales above SEK 600m in any quarter, supplier validation lifting the supply cap in H1 2027, or a larger acquisition would each raise estimates by mid-single digits.

What would change my view. Hyperscalers' 2027 capex guides in late January 2027 (a cut would bring the first cautious cue forward to the Q4 report); Corning's Q4 commentary on carrier and enterprise shipments; or a Data Center print below SEK 500m.

Market versus me. The broker and I expect the same two beats. The dashboard's November revision burst will look like fresh momentum, but it is not. The market has no published downside scenario and does not discuss the drop in growth when comparisons harden, so the surprises left in the case beyond April 2027 are mostly negative.

Score: 50. High near-term probability of beats and small estimate nudges against a thin consensus; no scope for a sustained annual upgrade cycle, a likely first cautious cue by mid-2027 and a 2029 figure that will come down.

#8Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, share price, and peers

Hexatronic's momentum is strong in the rear-view mirror and flattening in the windscreen.

Evidence. Every measure of momentum is positive over twelve months; most have flattened over the past three to five months.

Inference. The price trend is intact but has stalled since May (the stock has traded between SEK 38 and 44 for five months), revisions have paused pending follow-through from the Q3 report, the narrative is two thirds told, and the three largest Swedish institutions have sold into strength.

The stock now moves independently of its listed sector, but it remains exposed to AI-optics sentiment events that it cannot control. Its shareholder register is thinning at the top and broadening at the bottom, and such a register re-rates the stock on delivery and de-rates it on doubt.

So what. The technical setup is a consolidation inside an uptrend. The next catalysts (Corning's and Prysmian's results in the next two weeks, the Riksbank decision and the mechanical revision burst in November, and the 5 February report) are more likely to resolve the consolidation upward than downward over three months; the risk is an external AI-optics event. A clean break above SEK 45-49 on a Q4 beat would re-establish the trend; a failure at the 200-day average (SEK 36) would be the first technical sign that the market is pricing the mid-2027 drop in growth early.

Strongest counter-case. Nine months of a rising 200-day average, relative strength at the 95th percentile, and a stock that absorbed a 19% drawdown without breaking its trend make a textbook Stage 2 (advancing-phase) chart. The November revision burst and two beats could carry the stock to new highs, and the change in the register is passive money arriving, which tends to stay.

What would change my view. A Corning or Prysmian disappointment in the next two weeks that takes the cohort down 10%, and Hexatronic with it, would show that the sentiment channel dominates. A FactSet revision burst that lifts the sell-side rating to B, with the price breaking out, would show that the momentum phase has another leg.

Market versus me. The dashboard rates technical momentum B and sell-side momentum C, and I agree. I add two points the narrative does not carry: price momentum has been flat for five months, and the selling by domestic institutions is a signal.

Score: 60. Strong trailing price and estimate momentum, a conservative-cue pattern still intact and a weak peer group it has decoupled from; held back by five months of flat price, paused revisions, domestic selling and exposure to AI-optics sentiment events.

#9Riskiness and simplicity of forecasts and expectations

The case is moderately risky and moderately simple, and its predictability is front-loaded: narrow for two reports, wide thereafter.

Simplicity of the case. The drivers are countable and visible: three segments reported quarterly with organic growth and margin, a pre-report consensus, a four-month order book, and two external channels (US private fibre capex and hyperscaler capex) that account for about three quarters of the organic difference between the forecasts and the past. That makes the case simpler than in 2022, when one driver (FTTH duct volume and price) explained everything with decremental margins of 100%, and simpler than most Nordic small caps of its size.

The case is less simple than it looks, for four reasons: the two demand channels are correlated; the EPS bases differ (consensus, model and LTIP); reported EPS carries SEK 0.10-0.20 a year of noise from one-offs and revaluations; and the company's perimeter grows by three to six acquired units a year by policy.

What the base case requires. The base case needs seven things to go right, and each is a real test:

  • North American volume still growing from Q2 2027: the refill ends gently, not abruptly.
  • Data Center settling at SEK 550m quarters and growing 15%.
  • Fiber Solutions holding a 9.4% margin against duct price pressure, although no duct maker in the precedents held a recovered margin through the second year of recovery without price increases.
  • Glass and connector shortages restricting growth rather than removing it.
  • SEK 400m a year of acquisitions at about 6x EBITDA, without the departed architect of the acquisitions.
  • A permanent CFO and Data Center head appointed by February 2027.
  • The Hudiksvall permit and production line on time, despite four prior commissioning slips; SEK 100m of 2028 sales is at risk of a one-year slip.

The 18-month forecasts rest on demonstrated strengths. About a third of the 2028-30 forecasts rests on strengths still to be acquired, and about half of the company's 12% margin target does.

Share-price risks: suddenness, predictability, trackability, prevalence and materiality. The table below gives each fundamental risk's probability and impact over 18 months.

Suddenness is high for the US and hyperscaler channels and for supply allocation, and low for Europe and defence. Late 2025's 26% fall in North American sales was visible only when reported, and MasTec deferred USD 400m of work on one AT&T decision.

Predictability and trackability are moderate. The company discloses no order intake, book-to-bill ratio or split of price and volume, so the first signal of a turn will come from outside: Corning, Prysmian, Dura-Line, Clearfield, Dycom and MasTec, spot fibre prices and hyperscalers' guidance, with one to two quarters' lead. Hexatronic's disclosure is good for verifying a quarter and poor for anticipating a turn.

Perception risk is high and independent of fundamentals. Hexatronic is a small, thinly traded Swedish stock with one broker, it has doubled, it is tied to an AI theme whose financing has cracked, and the current regime penalises exactly this profile. A 20-35% drawdown on intact earnings is plausible; a trough multiple of 8-10x would put the shares 25-40% lower on intact earnings and 50-60% lower on trough earnings.

Sector and cyclicality, with precedents. The precedents are consistently harsh:

  • Fibre volumes overshoot and then destock for 18-24 months (2001; 2022-24).
  • Capacity lands into slowing demand and prices halve (Chinese fibre in 2018-21; high-voltage cable in 2016-20, when Nexans' and NKT's shares de-rated one to two quarters before their earnings fell).
  • Forecasts for the second year of recovery after a destock were met less often than not at duct and connectivity makers (Clearfield's fiscal 2026 cut; Dura-Line's 2024 price erosion; Hexatronic's own 2024-25 cuts).
  • The European cable sector's forward P/E de-rated 30% from its June 2026 peak while earnings were still rising, and HMS Networks fell on an in-line report.

Hexatronic's own history is the base rate. Against that history, a ±25% range on year-ahead EPS is tight, and that tightness is what the lower cost base, the three-cycle mix and the equity raise have bought.

Inference and so what. The case is easier to monitor than in 2022, and easier than the long list of company items suggests, because it reduces to two channels with observable external leads. It is harder than a typical Nordic industrial, because those two channels are correlated, are leveraged at 30-40% in the largest segment, and sit under a stock whose multiple is driven by the company's own story and whose precedent is to fall before earnings do. Predictability is front-loaded: narrow for two reports, wide thereafter. The practical risk management is therefore a dated monitoring plan rather than a wider valuation band: Corning in late October and late January; Prysmian on 29 October; the Riksbank in November; hyperscalers' guidance in late January; Hexatronic's reports on 5 February and in late April.

Strongest counter-case. Three cycles that do not move together, a direct US channel that has already weathered one distributor destock, a four-month order book, leverage of 1.3x and a demonstrated cost floor make Hexatronic materially less fragile than its 2023 self. The probability-weighted downside (about -40%, to SEK 24-26, on the first set of arithmetic) is smaller than the 2023-25 drawdown of more than 80%, and the base case survives either one of the two channels turning.

What would change my view. Disclosure of order intake or of a Fiber Solutions order book would raise trackability by a grade, and a second broker would reduce the dependence on a single model. A hyperscaler capex cut or a Brightspeed restructuring would raise the near-term probability of the correlated downside above 50%.

Market versus me. The narrative carries the supply constraint as a damper, the leadership changes lightly and the mid-2027 drop in growth only in outline. It does not carry a downside scenario, the correlation of the two channels, US duct price pressure or the noise from differing EPS bases. I am more cautious than the market on the prevalence and correlation of risks, and in line on the bounded near-term risk.

Score: 40. Simpler and better bounded than its own history and than the item count suggests, but two correlated external channels under 30-40% operating leverage, no forward disclosure, a thin one-broker register and a sector precedent of de-rating before earnings fall make it riskier than the median European listed company.

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

The honest placement is "thesis broadening, not yet reinforcing": one phase below the dashboard's rule, and the phase sets the multiple.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule places the stock in the "Reinforcing" phase. The facts behind the placement are mixed:

  • Estimates are up 16% over twelve months and flat over three, after four beats.
  • The multiple is at its ten-year median (13.2-13.8x) and at the 80th percentile of the past two years, up from 5x.
  • The share price is up 113% over twelve months but flat for five months.
  • One broker is visible, and the narrative is two thirds told.
  • The dashboard's eight master ratings at 22 October are: Change Forces B, Foundations C, Fit B, Riskiness C, Sell-side C, Thematic D, Technical B and TSR/Valuation D.
  • The three largest Swedish institutions are reducing their holdings.
  • The next two reports are bounded and likely beats, but by the company's own cues the growth rate starts to decelerate in H1 2027, and competitors' capacity is scheduled for 2027-28.

Inference. The "bottoming" phase ended in 2025, and the "turning up" phase is complete: the trough-on-trough setup (5-8x on depressed earnings) has been harvested, and the shares trade at a median multiple on recovered earnings.

The "Reinforcing" phase, as the framework defines it (estimates rising broadly, the multiple expanding on delivery, the narrative widening to new holders), is only partly present. Estimates rose and have paused; the multiple expanded and has stalled at the median; the narrative has one author; and the domestic holders are selling. "Stalling" is not yet visible in the fundamentals, and would show first in North American growth in Q2-Q3 2027 or in a Data Center quarter below SEK 500m.

The business has broadened the thesis beyond FTTH (into data centres, defence, subsea, US localisation and acquisitions) and has proved delivery for eighteen months, but the market has not yet granted it the next phase. The twelve months after April 2027 decide the outcome: either Hexatronic earns the next phase by holding a margin floor through hard comparisons, which would justify a higher multiple for its changed mix, or it reverts to the cyclical template.

So what. The phase placement is the hinge of the valuation. A "Reinforcing" phase carries a guideline multiple of 22.34x; a "thesis broadening" placement would, in my judgement, carry a guideline nearer the 75th percentile (17.6x); and a "turning up" placement would carry the median or below. I use the thesis-broadening reading and set my fair range accordingly in #11. In practice, the next two reports are the window in which the stock can advance a phase; a cautious cue in mid-2027 would move it toward "stalling", and the multiple would fall before the earnings did.

Strongest counter-case. The dashboard rule is mechanical, and the momentum and revision facts it uses are positive. Four beats of rising size, a record year ahead, a 200-day average rising for nine months and a buy share of 75% are the signature of a reinforcing phase; the paused revisions are a data lag that November will correct; and the mix pivot is precisely what moves a stock from cyclical-recovery to compounder pricing, as HMS Networks and Lagercrantz show.

What would change my view. Two beats and a FactSet revision burst, with a second broker initiating coverage by April 2027, would move me to "Reinforcing". A Data Center print below SEK 500m, North American growth in single digits or a defensive capacity cut would move me to "Stalling".

Market versus me. The dashboard says "Reinforcing"; Redeye's framing ("no longer a deep discount", base-case value SEK 46) is consistent with a stock most of the way through its re-rating; the forums follow the price. I sit between the dashboard and the broker.

Score: 58. Past the turn with delivery proven and the thesis genuinely broader than a year ago, but not yet in a broad-based reinforcing phase: one broker, paused revisions, a median multiple, domestic sellers and a known deceleration ahead.

#11The fair multiple

My fair range is 13.6-17.6x (the median to the 75th percentile) on consensus-basis two-year-forward EPS, with a central 15.5x, well below the 22.34x guideline.

The guideline. Viewforth's guideline multiple for the dashboard's "Reinforcing" phase is 22.34x two-year-forward earnings, the 90th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history (bands: 10th percentile 8.2x, 35th 11.7x, median 13.6x, 75th 17.6x, 90th 22.3x). The guideline is 69% above the 13.2x on which the stock trades. The stock traded at 22x or more only from April 2021 to December 2022, when organic growth exceeded 60%, the margin was 16-17% and investors believed FTTH to be a decade-long structural build; the multiple fell from 42x to 5x in two years when that belief broke.

My view. The guideline marks the top of the plausible range, not the central case, for four reasons:

  1. Phase. On the evidence in #10 the stock is thesis-broadening, not reinforcing. The 90th percentile belongs to a stock in peak delivery with a widening holder base and rising estimates, and Hexatronic is not yet that stock.
  2. Quality. A mid-quality cyclical in a competitive downstream layer, with no real pricing power, 10-12% returns on capital, a margin plateau at 11% and growth that is half bought, earns a cyclical-recovery multiple, not a compounder's. The precedents that sustained bands of 20x or more (Invisio at 20-50x EV/EBITDA, HMS Networks at 24-30x EV/EBIT, Kitron's defence premium) had organic growth of 20-44% or a fifteen-year acquisition record.
  3. Direction of the forecasts. The rate of change has peaked, the range of outcomes widens from mid-2027 with a negative skew, and competitors' capacity arrives in 2028. The framework itself says that the fair multiple is lower where forecasts are more uncertain, and in stalling or turning phases.
  4. Basis. The stock's historical multiples were struck on consensus-basis EPS, so any multiple drawn from that history must be applied to consensus-basis EPS (SEK 3.58 for 2029), not to the model's pre-amortisation SEK 4.28.

Why a central 15.5x. The central 15.5x pays a modest premium to the median, because Hexatronic has a structurally better mix, a lower cost base, a contracted subsea step-up and a less levered balance sheet than at any point in its ten-year history. It sits at a discount to the 75th percentile because of the cyclical core, the thin register and the dated expiry of the industry's support. Redeye's 9.1x EV/EBITA for 2027 is consistent with about 14-15x P/E on Redeye's own 2027 EPS.

What would move the band. If the next twelve months prove the Fiber Solutions margin floor through hard comparisons and a second broker arrives, the 75th percentile (17.6x) becomes defensible. If Q2-Q3 2027 show the US refill ending, the fair multiple falls to the 35th percentile (11.7x) or below, and the stock's own precedent is to overshoot to 8-10x.

Strongest counter-case. The ten-year history includes 2016-20, when the company was an FTTH duct maker with sales below SEK 2bn trading at 12-19x. Today's business is three times that size, half of it in structural data-centre and defence niches, with a serial acquirer's cadence. The right comparison set might be the Nordic serial acquirers (HMS Networks at 24x, Lagercrantz and Lifco higher), in which case 18-22x is not mania. The dashboard's valuation rating of C (52nd percentile) also says that the stock is not expensive on its own history.

What would change my view. A Fiber Solutions margin above 10% and a group margin above 11.5% through Q3 2027, Data Center proving that re-cabling recurs, a second or third broker, or a capital-return decision in 2029 would each move my central multiple toward 17.6x. A cautious cue in mid-2027 would move it toward 11.7x.

Market versus me. The market pays 13.2-13.8x, the stock's own median; the broker's base-case value (SEK 46) implies about 14-16x on its 2028 EPS; the guideline says 22.34x. I am with the market and the broker, modestly above today's multiple, and well below the guideline.

Score: 50. The guideline multiple is generous for the phase and the business quality; my own fair range sits only modestly above today's multiple, so valuation is neither a tailwind nor a headwind of note.

#12Total shareholder return (Dupont: earnings growth, change in the multiple, dividends)

The probability-weighted value at end-2027 is about SEK 47 a share, +15%; earnings growth of about +21% is the bedrock of the return, and the multiple is the swing.

The model's return at the guideline multiple. The one-page summary gives a return of +133.3% to the 18-month column (31 December 2027; value SEK 95.52; 104.6% annualised) and +167.0% to the three-year column (30 June 2029; value SEK 109.30; 44.2% annualised), with zero dividends. The SEK 95.52 is 22.34x applied to the model's FY2029 EPS of SEK 4.28. The SEK 109.30 is 22.34x applied to about SEK 4.89, the model's two-year-forward EPS at mid-2029 (a blend of FY2030's SEK 4.71 and an extrapolated FY2031).

The summary's split of the return into dividends, multiple and earnings (-142.2%, -652.5% and similar figures) is the template's own output and cannot be interpreted, so I rebuild the decomposition below. The driver of the model's number is clear: a multiple move from 11.3x (the model's own two-year-forward multiple today, on its basis) to 22.34x (about +98%), multiplied by two-year-forward EPS growth from about SEK 3.6 to SEK 4.28 (about +18%). Three things inflate the result: the EPS is pre-amortisation (SEK 0.70 above the consensus basis in 2029), the revenue-base artefact adds about SEK 0.22 a share, and the multiple is the ten-year 90th percentile applied to a stock at its median.

What drives the return. Over 14 months, earnings growth alone is worth about +21%, and more on a clean basis (the 2026 base holds SEK 0.23 of one-off gain), so the stock delivers a mid-teens to high-teens return with no re-rating at all. That earnings growth is the bedrock of the case, and it is the part with the highest probability, because most of it sits in the two easy quarters. The multiple is the swing: from -41% to +62% across the stock's own ten-year bands. Dividends contribute nothing before 2030. Over three years, earnings compound at about 12% a year on the consensus basis (more slowly than EBITA, because of amortisation and the higher share count), and the multiple decides whether the annualised return is 12% or 30%.

Scenario-weighted value. I weight the three 2027 scenarios (27% downside, 55% base, 18% upside) and give each a matching multiple. Downside: two-year-forward EPS of about SEK 2.9 at 9x, SEK 26 a share. Base: SEK 3.58 at 13.6-15.5x, SEK 49-56, say SEK 52. Upside: 2029 EPS of about SEK 4.2 at 17.6x, SEK 74, cut to SEK 65 for the probability that the multiple lags. The probability-weighted value at end-2027 is about SEK 47 (+15%), with a range of -36% to +60%. The expected return is positive, the distribution is wide and twin-peaked, and most of the probability of a positive outcome is front-loaded into the first six months.

Strongest counter-case. If the market moves to a serial-acquirer or mix-change framing after two beats, 17.6-20x on SEK 3.58-3.9 gives SEK 63-78 by end-2027, and the model's SEK 95 becomes reachable in the upside scenario if a second broker models 2029 at the guideline multiple. The 2023 precedent cuts both ways: in 2020-21 the multiple travelled from 7x to 42x on a believed end-market.

What would change my view. The same tests as in #11: the Fiber Solutions margin floor through H2 2027, the Data Center level, a second broker, and the external leads. A Q4 2026 beat with a Data Center print above SEK 580m would raise my central multiple toward 17x and the 14-month value toward SEK 61.

Market versus me. The broker's base-case value of SEK 46 (+12%) is below my central SEK 55 because the broker applies a lower multiple to a similar EPS; the model's SEK 95.52 is above it because of the EPS basis and the multiple. I sit between the two, closer to the broker.

Score: 52. A positive expected return (about +15% weighted, +36% central over 14 months) driven mainly by near-term earnings growth, with no dividend support and a multiple that is as likely to subtract as to add from mid-2027.

#13Summary conclusion

Hexatronic is a well-run recovery with a cyclical core, not a compounder, and its positive skew is real but dated.

The internal change is real and has reached the accounts. The external tailwinds are strong but cyclical, capped by supply and past their peak rate of change. The favourable industry structure is borrowed rather than owned. The forecasts are credible: in line with the one broker for 2026-28, below it for 2029, and front-loaded into an easy first half of 2027.

The investment case over the next 6-18 months is therefore two cases joined at the Q1 2027 report. The first is a high-probability, bounded six months, in which the company beats a thin, company-set consensus twice and about 20% earnings growth supports the shares even without a re-rating. The second is a lower-probability, negatively skewed twelve months, in which the market learns three things: whether the Fiber Solutions margin floor survives hard comparisons and US duct price pressure; whether Data Center's run-rate is SEK 550m or SEK 650m a quarter; and whether the two correlated demand channels hold through a discount-rate shock and an AI financing scare.

The stock trades at its own median multiple, which is roughly fair, and the guideline multiple of 22.34x overstates both the phase and the quality. My central value is SEK 55 at end-2027 (+36%), my probability-weighted value about SEK 47 (+15%), and my scenario range roughly SEK 26-65.

The positive skew that Richard looks for exists, but it is dated: it lies in the November revision burst and the February and April reports. A holder beyond April 2027 is underwriting the upside scenario (supply eases, BEAD orders arrive, Data Center holds its level, 2027 EPS reaches SEK 3.2) against the company's own 2023 precedent that the multiple moves before the earnings. The tripwires are external and observable, which is the constructive point: this case can be managed by calendar, not by hope.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: B. Strong external forces (the AI data-centre build, the US rebuild, defence) and internal forces (cost, mix pivot, acquisitions, balance sheet) have already reached the profit line; the rating falls short of A because the external forces are cyclical and dated, the self-help is complete and the management bench has thinned.

Foundations' Robustness: C. A mid-quality cyclical in a competitive downstream layer with no upstream position, 10-12% returns on capital, heavy working capital and a margin ceiling below the last peak, offset by a lower cost base, three uncorrelated demand cycles, a direct US channel and a clean balance sheet.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: C. The 2025 trough-on-trough setup (the framework's "CfC in a quality cyclical") has been harvested, with the multiple back at the median. What remains is a hybrid of two EPS-upgrade (EPSU) setups, one driven by big corporate change (largely delivered) and one driven by demand (capped by supply and negatively skewed from mid-2027), plus a serial-acquirer element too small and too young to work mechanically. The fit is real but not crisp.

Case Riskiness: C. Simpler and better bounded than its own history, with observable external leads and a four-month order book, but two correlated external channels under 30-40% operating leverage, no forward disclosure, a thin one-broker register, and a sector precedent of de-rating one to two quarters before earnings fall.

Appendix A: how to read the numbers in this memo

Three EPS bases are in play, and only the consensus basis may be combined with the stock's historical multiples.

This memo names the EPS basis every time it quotes one.

  • Consensus basis: reported diluted EPS after amortisation of acquired intangibles. Redeye and FactSet carry this basis, and the Financial Analyst's cross-check uses it.
  • Model basis: the Excel model's adjusted EPS, which leaves out the amortisation of acquired intangibles and so sits SEK 0.35-0.45 a share higher every year.
  • Clean 2026: SEK 2.20, which strips out the SEK 67m reversal of the Clinton impairment booked in Q3 2026 (about SEK 0.23 a share after tax). Both Redeye's SEK 2.39 and our SEK 2.38 contain that reversal.

The forecasts of record. The forecasts of record are the model's inputs (revenue growth and EBITDA margin), applied to the company's own FY2025 revenue base of SEK 7,519m; the base-case table in #6 shows the resulting revenue and adjusted EBITA.

The revenue-base artefact. The one-page summary's revenue line (SEK 8,986m for 2026, "+24%") carries a mechanical artefact: the summary applied the quarterly growth rates to FactSet's quarterly history, which runs 5-8% above the company's own quarters. Every year's revenue in that line is therefore about 3.6% too high, and EBITA SEK 38-67m too high. No input is wrong; the base needs rebasing.

The rule for multiples. Multiples drawn from the consensus-basis history (the dashboard's 13.8x and its ten-year percentiles) must be applied to consensus-basis EPS, never to model-basis EPS.

End notes

Default charts and tables come from FactSet, the Master Dashboard and the one-page summary of the Financial Analyst's model; each carries its own basis in its note. Charts in the drawn set take their figures from the memo text. Where the memo gives a range, the chart shows its midpoint or the full range, as labelled.

The quarterly chart in #6 derives Q2 and Q3 2026 sales and the Q2 2026 margin from the base case's year-on-year growth rates and its H1 and H2 2027 EBITA. The model's own split of total shareholder return into dividends, multiple and earnings is not shown, because #12 explains it cannot be interpreted; the rebuilt decomposition is shown instead.

Abbreviations: BABA, the US Build America, Buy America Act; BEAD, the US Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment programme; FTTH, fibre to the home; HDPE, high-density polyethylene; LTIP, long-term incentive plan; MPO, multi-fibre push-on (a connector type); TSR, total shareholder return.

Grades: A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24.

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

  • Consensus EBIT for FY2026 is 734.00, +891.9% against 74.00 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves +17.5%.

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:
